newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end lacklustre day lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end lacklustre day lower.

text.p: *Stocks end lower after Dow volatility keeps local investors nervous. Trade still at holiday levels. Volume 297.25 million, value A$486.59 million,970 stocks traded, 339 steady, 277 rises, 354 falls
The Australian share market closed lower on Friday after a volatile Wall Street kept local investors nervous.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 11.7 points lower at 2,399.5.
March share price index futures were down 17 points at 2,419 and were at a 19.5 point premium to the underlying index.

The market muddled about within a six-point range for all but the first 30 minutes of trade in the last day of the Christmas-New Year hiatus. Brokers volumes remained subdued with many players still away.

"The market was a bit lower which was not altogether surprising on the back of what we got from overseas, but we won't have a return to normal trading until Monday," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely, pointing to the dull day's lack of activity.

Among the bigger stocks, retailers suffered late in the day after upmarket department store operator David Jones slashed its profit forecast, citing continued depressed conditions in the retail sector. Shares in rival operator, Coles Myer, also softened after the David Jones announcement.

Kingstream Resources sparked some activity early after the company said it planned to merge with An Feng Steel Co Ltd, its Taiwan-based partner in the proposed A$1.4 billion Midwest Iron and Steel project in Western Australia.
Kingstream shares closed seven cents higher at A$1.02.

Westpac Banking shares featured in the turnover list with a total of 14.5 million shares valued at A$102.6 million traded, making the market's turnover look more impressive than it really was. The bulk of the Westpac trade was in several crossings in the morning and special trades after the market closed with brokers saying the activity was dividend-related.
Outlook remained mixed with Wall Street likely to remain the focus of attention in the absence of any major domestic news.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade continued at moderate levels although options trade remained slow.
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 5,678 (5,958)
In other local markets, a weakening technical picture saw Australian bond futures fall further during the afternoon and the market overshoot Thursday's sharp sell-off in U.S. debt.

Uncertainty over the US outlook gave domestic bonds a nasty jolt in the first few days of 1997 with long US yields rising 20 basis points in the last two trading sessions. Locally, 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.69 percent by 4.35 p.m. (0535 GMT).

The Australian dollar reclaimed some lost ground in a thin market, stabilising above US$0.7900 after a half-cent fall overnight. Trade was affected by Japan's closure but liquidity should return to more normal levels next week as Tokyo reopens and the first major data of the year are released.
By 4.35 p.m. (0535 GMT) the Australian dollar was at US$0.7915/20 up on its opening US$0.7908/13.
